title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government outlines its stance and action plan in response to the 2020 Committee report on Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards. It commits to improving regulation, promoting transparency, and supporting research to ensure AI benefits society.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out rules to oversee how artificial intelligence can be used in creating, marking and validating qualifications, with the aim of safeguarding fairness, quality and security in assessment. The policy, issued after a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade, will establish guidelines, standards and monitoring procedures to ensure AI tools support rather than compromise the integrity of the qualifications sector.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: The report examines how copyright works are used to train AI systems, assessing the legal, economic, and ethical impacts of that practice. It offers recommendations for balancing creators’ rights with AI innovation to protect intellectual property while encouraging technological advancement.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government has issued a response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence’s report titled “AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency.” It outlines plans and measures to address AI‑related concerns, emphasizing the UK’s commitment to safe, ethical, and competitive AI use.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the responsibilities and objectives of a committee tasked with reviewing artificial intelligence in the context of public standards. It includes the terms of reference and frequently asked questions to guide the committee's work.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry on the governance of Artificial Intelligence, outlining its concerns and recommendations. The submission highlights the need for clear regulatory frameworks, transparency, and accountability to guide responsible AI development and deployment.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy examines how artificial intelligence will shape the rules governing medical products, proposing updated standards and oversight to keep pace with technological advances. It aims to implement the AI White Paper’s principles, ensuring that medical devices are safe, effective, and transparent while meeting evolving regulatory requirements.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy aims to make the organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI‑driven defence group in the world, relative to its size. It focuses on building AI capabilities, setting standards, and forging partnerships to achieve that goal.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness AI’s benefits, such as improving safety, efficiency, and innovation. It also details measures to address risks, including privacy, security, and ethical concerns, ensuring responsible AI deployment across the sector.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report examines how copyright-protected works are being used to train and develop AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It evaluates current practices, identifies challenges and opportunities, and offers recommendations to balance copyright protection with AI innovation.
